_note: Values that encode a DECISION rather than a measurement. tools/check_decisions.py recomputes each from its real source and REFUSES if one has moved, because a decision changing is exactly the case where a deliberate act should be required — and editing this file in the same commit is that act. Most numbers in this build move every run; these do not. See own error 48.

kitPin.why: Which build of the shared kit this archive's gates are. It moved inside a commit about gating a chart on 27 September and three builds passed over it unnoticed — own error 48. MOVED 13 OCTOBER 2026 to 8fdc6b0, which fixes a fault this archive reported after its own move: kit/styles/print.css hard-coded daviddef.github.io into the address it prints beside every internal link, so every archive on its own domain PRINTED the wrong site — on paper, where a URL matters most because the reader has to type it. A plain CSS file cannot know which archive it is printing, so print.css now emits the path alone and SocialHead, which every page renders, overrides it with the origin from archives.json. The predecessor 281c8d6 carried the rest of the estate's moves to their own domains, and before it e275c14 added whoami(), which settles which archive is being built by ORIGIN rather than by base. MOVED 16 OCTOBER 2026 to 3efc89e, whose sitemap leaves out a page whose canonical names another page; moved on its own in a commit that touches only the pin files and this record.

siteOrigin.why: Where this archive lives, stated in three files that must agree: astro.config.mjs's `site`, site/public/CNAME and site/public/robots.txt's Sitemap line. MOVED 12 OCTOBER 2026 from daviddef.github.io/TheDArcy, because defranceski.com is a Pages site served by its own repo and project paths do not inherit it — defranceski.com/TheDArcy/ returns 404 — so a subdomain was the only route. THE CHECK EXISTS BECAUSE THE MOVE LEFT ONE OF THE THREE BEHIND. robots.txt went on naming a sitemap at the old origin while everything else had moved; the build was green and every gate passed, because no gate read it. A reader would never notice and a crawler reads nothing else. CNAME is the dangerous one: this repo deploys by Actions uploading site/dist, and a deploy carrying no CNAME DETACHES the custom domain, so a wrong or missing one takes the whole archive dark rather than leaving a stale line. The gate does not judge whether the address is right — nobody here can — only whether the three agree, and all three failure modes were provoked and seen to refuse before it was trusted.

livingPolicy.why: named-place: a living person is named, with their town and country, and nothing more. MOVED 16 OCTOBER 2026 from named-bare-by-omission (no living person published as a person at all; the key was absent and people.js's fallback was doing the work) on David's ruling, made knowing the tree judges 2,034 people living: this archive adopts the standard the Defranceschi archive keeps. The key is now present in living.json and people.js falls back to the same string.

namedLiving.why: The six living people named on purpose in prose, confirmed deliberately by David (14 and 15 September 2026). Anyone appearing or disappearing here is a change to who this archive names on purpose. They are unchanged by the 16 October 2026 standard; every other living person is now named too, and that is the policy above, not this list.

grafts.why: The two rejected links and how many people hang off each. /how-far-back publishes these counts in a sentence — 71 on a single unevidenced link, 27 on a disproved one — so if the tree moves, that sentence goes stale.

retiredAllow.why: The pages allowed to restate a withdrawn reading, because their subject IS the withdrawal. Widening this list quietly would disarm the retired-reading gate.

livingExemptions.why: Every phrase the living gate is told to let through — the union of living.json's `named`, `namesakes` and `allow`. namedLiving watches who this archive decided to publish; this watches the whole exemption surface, because a phrase added to namesakes is exempted just as effectively and nothing else here would say so.

heldOutIds.why: David's ruling of 16 October 2026: the living woman whose DNA result the archive describes is HELD OUT. She stays as she was before the living standard: no page, no record, no name as anybody's relative, nothing in a file the site serves or the repository tracks that could be traced to her. /dna/ says she is not named, and that sentence has to stay true. Held by id only; no file, message or log names her. tools/check_living_standard.py proves the id is absent from every data file and built page; tools/check_living.py, which reads the tree, proves her name is too.

value.dna-tester: held by id; a living person whose DNA result the archive describes without naming her
value.possible-minor: a living person with no birth year in the tree who has a living parent

heldOutRules.why: David's ruling of 16 October 2026: every living person with no birth year in the tree who has a living parent is HELD OUT, because without a year nobody can tell a child from an adult, and a child is not named. A rule, not a list of names: tools/gedcom.held_out() decides it from the tree, tools/build_site_data.py and tools/ancestry.py both use it, and tools/check_living.py recomputes it independently and proves not one of them has a page, a record, or a name as anybody's relative. The count of how many were met and left out is written to living.json and printed, never their names.

recordedDeadKinds.why: David's ruling of 16 October 2026: a person the tree RECORDS as deceased is dead whether or not a date exists. MyHeritage writes a death event with no date for somebody it knows to be dead and does not know when; a burial says the same. Before that day the build ignored such a record unless it carried a date and judged the person living, so 544 people in the tree were judged living though the tree itself said otherwise. They are ordinary dead people now: no 'treated as living' wording, indexable pages, and no date or field they do not already hold in the tree. The 100-year upper-bound test still applies to everyone NOT recorded as dead.
